title: meta-analysis.cz: harmonised estimate-level data from meta-analyses in economics
description:
Estimate-level data from 46 economics meta-analyses, and a pooled table that stacks 42 of them into one schema. Every value is traceable to the published file it came from, and every published file is the one its authors released.

What this release contains. 67,606 rows across the 46 converted source files. The pooled table carries 53,341 estimates, of which 49,535 lie inside the analysis samples the source papers themselves define. The paper-sample figure is the one a citation should use; the larger figure counts every estimate carried, including those a paper excluded, and those are flagged rather than hidden.

2.0.0 is a breaking release. Three things changed that will alter results computed against 1.3.0.

1. Estimates a paper excluded are now carried, not deleted. Where a paper's replication code defines a row filter, the excluded rows enter the table with in_paper_sample false and paper_sample_exclusion naming the clause that removed them, so a reader can test an exclusion instead of taking it on trust. Reproduce any paper's own sample by filtering in_paper_sample to true. Not every filter was treated this way, and the distinction matters: a clause that defines which literature a row belongs to still deletes, because bma and spillovers are two papers over one collection partitioned by a single column and lifting it would have placed the same estimates in the table twice; and electricity's clause removing 117 rows whose standard errors are imputed still deletes, because carrying fabricated precision into a publication-bias dataset would be worse than dropping it.

2. A second effect scale is carried where a paper analyses one. effect_alt, se_alt, effect_alt_units and effect_alt_role. A row now enters on either scale, so an estimate expressible only on the alternative scale is published for the first time; on those rows effect is null and effect_alt carries the estimate. The former pcc and se_pcc columns are retired: they duplicated effect in seven of the eight datasets that filled them.

3. Three literatures changed what they publish, after an audit compared all 46 datasets against the full text of their own papers.

  • class published the partial correlation of an appendix robustness block as its effect. The headline scale is now the change in test scores in hundredths of a standard deviation per additional student, which is the metric the paper's main models use; the partial correlation is kept as the alternative scale. Anyone who used class in 1.3.0 or earlier was analysing the robustness metric.
  • activism published 20 estimates with the wrong sign, and reached only 1,254 rows of the 1,851 available, because the pipeline reconstructed the effect and the standard error instead of reading the columns the authors published. Now 1,851 estimates over 55 studies, and the median matches the paper's own reported figure.
  • armington featured the raw reported pair, which cannot reproduce its paper's own publication-bias result. The winsorised pair is now the headline and the raw pair the alternative scale.

Also corrected: size had no standard error mapped at all; forward, scc and price_puzzle were counted as analysing more than they do, now flagged rather than removed.

What has not changed. The source files, the round-trip guarantee that every harmonised value occurs in its original published file, and the licence. Everything here is CC BY 4.0.
notes: Everything in this deposit is released under CC BY 4.0, as is everything on meta-analysis.cz: the datasets, their CSV and Parquet conversions, the pooled table, the codebooks, the documentation and the deposited papers. You may use, adapt and redistribute any of it for any purpose, including commercially and including as training data for machine-learning models. The only condition is credit: cite the individual paper when you use its dataset, and the collection when you use the whole.
